### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/rest`, touching **58** documentable anchor(s).

**42** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f5e23e2f7c570d14da0f012e0857f4be7c6636d2`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 51 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **70** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f5e23e2f7c570d14da0f012e0857f4be7c6636d2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3fb8dfc78b220a7f8ead8d0d9b503436203ce7a0` — the merge of head `94ee3ead4260b2f9e77423a52a5d4ef64797d719` into base `f5e23e2f7c570d14da0f012e0857f4be7c6636d2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3fb8dfc78b220a7f8ead8d0d9b503436203ce7a0 && git checkout 3fb8dfc78b220a7f8ead8d0d9b503436203ce7a0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f5e23e2f7c570d14da0f012e0857f4be7c6636d2 94ee3ead4260b2f9e77423a52a5d4ef64797d719 && git checkout -B drift-repro f5e23e2f7c570d14da0f012e0857f4be7c6636d2 && git merge --no-ff 94ee3ead4260b2f9e77423a52a5d4ef64797d719

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f5e23e2f7c570d14da0f012e0857f4be7c6636d2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f5e23e2f7c570d14da0f012e0857f4be7c6636d2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `94ee3ead4260b2f9e77423a52a5d4ef64797d719`

Inputs read: card #31215 (body; comments 6711625441, 6711801309, 6711840578, 6711854159, 6715940083, 6716292410), PR #31336 (body, 16-file list, `git diff origin/main...94ee3ead`), the head's check-runs, and the published contract on `main` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts`: `describeEffectiveAccess?`, `EffectiveAccess`, `EffectivePermissionSet`, `EffectivePermissionSetOrigin`, landed by #31256). Code outside the diff (`resolve-user-grants-cache.ts`, `request-grants-memo.ts`, `builtin-positions.ts`, `external-baseline.ts`, `explain-engine.ts#readSysUserRow`, `query-allowlist.ts`, the sibling `my-delegable-scope` door) was read to judge the diff, never reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

**The four things the contract docblock binds the implementer to — each judged one by one:**

1. **Resolution order — right.** The contract orders `permissionSets` as grant-row sets in grant order, then position-bound sets in held-position order, then the derived names (`admin_full_access`, then `ai_seat`), then the human baseline, a set already listed keeping its first place. `security-plugin-effective-access.ts` walks `grants.permissions` as the resolver built it (`take()` folds grant rows before `boundSetNames`; §6b-config pushes `ADMIN_FULL_ACCESS`; §7 pushes `ai_seat`) and appends `humanBaselineFor(...)` last as `default`; `byName` dedupes so a later arrival only adds an origin. `positions` is `[...grants.positions]` — the resolver's own list, with `platform_admin` unshifted first (6c), `everyone` pushed only for a non-external member, and switched-off positions already filtered. Pinned by the first, third, fifth and sixth cases of `effective-access.test.ts`.
2. **Unknown-user refusal — right.** One constructor, `effectiveAccessRefusal()`, with no id and no details, is thrown for a caller the gate refuses, for an id `readSysUserRow` finds no row for, and for an empty id; the existence read runs only after the gate, so a refused caller learns nothing about which ids exist; a `manage_users` caller asking about an unknown id gets that same refusal, not explain's `ExplainUserNotFoundError` 404 (ablation 1 in the PR body turned exactly that case red). The REST door maps it to one `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` whose body is pinned byte-identical across a known and an unknown id and contains no id.
3. **`external_default` placement — right.** The resolver records `{ kind: 'position', position: 'org_external' }` from `setsInForceByPosition` because `builtin-positions.ts` on `main` registers `org_external` with `permissionSets: [external_default]` into the catalog that `positionBoundSetNames` reads, and `humanBaselineFor` answers `[external_default]` for an external holder, which the service appends as `default`. `everyone` is never a `position` origin: its bindings are recorded as `default` at the one derivation site. The sixth test pins both origins on one entry and `everyone` absent from `positions`.
4. **What `positions` lists — right.** Exactly the resolver's list, in force, derived `platform_admin` leading, membership projections and own rows next, `everyone` last for a non-external member; the fifth test pins `platform_admin` first and the sixth pins `['org_external']` alone.

**Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies:**

- **New REST door** `GET {basePath}/security/users/:id/effective-access` (`security-routes.ts`, through the family's one `respondError` emitter) — right. Refusal order 401 (no `userId`, service never called) → 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` for any query parameter, from the empty closed set `EFFECTIVE_ACCESS_QUERY_PARAMS` via `unknownQueryParamRefusalMessage` (the helper whose docblock names own-envelope doors as its callers; the handler reads no other key of `req.query`, so the set measured from its read points is empty, AGENTS.md route rule 5) → 501 `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` when `!svc || typeof svc.describeEffectiveAccess !== 'function'`, the same shape and wording pattern as `my-delegable-scope` → bare relay of the service's object → 403 matched by `code`/`name` as explain matches it → `classifiedRefusalAnswer` → 500. Ledger row `disposition: 'sdk'`, `client: 'security.describeEffectiveAccess'`, family `security-explain`; the client-side ledger coverage test resolves that path to a real function. The registrar docblock in `rest-server.ts` names the route. Seven route tests pin registration, bare relay with `(id, caller)`, 401, byte-identical 403, 400 naming the parameter, 501 for both a member-less service and no provider, and 500.
- **Client method** `security.describeEffectiveAccess(userId)` — right. Returns `EffectiveAccess` through `unwrapResponse`, `encodeURIComponent(userId)` in the path; `return-type-precision.test.ts` pins `toEqualTypeOf` against `EffectiveAccess` and a `@ts-expect-error` wrong-shape assignment. `exported-any-returns.json` needs no entry (annotated return).
- **New service method** `SecurityPlugin#describeEffectiveAccess` — right. Bound on the class and on the registered literal, which is typed against `ISecurityService`, so the optional member's signature is compiler-checked; `EffectiveAccessHost` types every member it reads as the class member. Self-read needs no gate (the contract's "or the caller's own"); every other id goes through `mayDescribeAnotherUser`. Organization: the caller's `tenantId`, re-resolved under `vetOrganizationClaim` exactly as explain does (`buildContextForUser` twice there, `resolveIn` twice here), answered as `organizationId ?? null`. A name in `grants.permissions` without an origin throws a fault rather than inventing one — correct, since the service passes no `seedPermissions`, the one channel the docblock exempts. `registered-security-service-members.pin.test.ts` is unaffected: the member is declared on the interface.
- **`resolveUserAuthzGrants` in `@objectstack/core`** — right; **no existing caller's answer moves.** `withPermissionOrigins` builds `cacheOpts = { ...opts, bypassGrantsCache: true }`; both `openRequestGrantsMemo` and `openUserGrantsCache` return `undefined` on `bypassGrantsCache` before any read, so an origin-bearing envelope is neither served from nor committed to either cache — a later caller without the option can never receive `permissionOrigins`. Without the option: `origins` is `undefined`, `recordOrigin` is a no-op, the position loop iterates the same Map (entries in place of values), and the `ai_seat` branch condition `!includes('ai_seat') || origins` reduces to the old one. Every `grants.permissions` push site has an origin record: grant rows (`direct`, when active), position-bound (`position` or `default` for `everyone`), §6b-config (`derived: platform_admin_config`), §7 (`derived: ai_seat`); the final pass keeps origins only for names the envelope holds, so a disabled or body-less set keeps none. Pinned by the three new core cases, including byte-identical envelope and identical read sequence with and without the option.
- **Refactor of `security-plugin-explain-access.ts`** — right; one gate, one spelling. `mayDescribeAnotherUser` carries the old inline block verbatim in order: `isSystem` short-circuit, `resolvePermissionSetsForContext` with its `.catch` answering an empty list, `manage_users`, `organizationAdminCoversUser` with its `.catch` answering `false`, then `scopesCoverUser` with its `.catch` answering `false`. Explain calls it in place of the inline copy and throws the same `PermissionDeniedError` text with the same `{ object, operation, targetUserId }` details, then its own `readSysUserRow` → 404 unchanged. Explain's answer moves for no caller. The system-context census (`content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` row 9 and register) is regenerated to name both functions, with `explainAccessForCaller` down from 2 reads to 1.
- **Card acceptance** — met: three origins listed with the right kind (test 1), CONTROL direct-only user lists exactly one (test 2), a set reached by a direct row and two positions listed once with all three origins (test 3), anonymous 401 at the door, non-admin 403, unknown user byte-identical to forbidden for a member caller and for a `manage_users` caller, empty id likewise.
- **Security** — the read lists nothing beyond what the caller gate allows: the gate precedes the existence read and the resolution, the refusal names no id, the self-read path still requires a row, and the organization the sets are resolved in is vetted as explain vets it.

Findings: no must-fix. Should-fix: none. Nit (no effect on correctness or contract): `security-explain-envelope.test.ts` (#8073, "the whole explain family reduces to ONE skeleton") is not extended to the new door; the new route tests cover every arm through the same emitter, so the skeleton holds by construction.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/31215-effective-access-read.md` declares `patch` for `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/client` — exactly the four published packages (all 18.3.0, none private) whose files the diff touches; the other changed paths (`content/docs/...`, `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`, the changeset itself) publish nothing. `Metadata-protocol: none`, so the level is `patch` by AGENTS.md checklist 3 ("`none` takes patch"); `Clause-②: yes` is line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset body, with no arm, which is the right declaration for a widening of the served HTTP surface that narrows nothing. `packages/spec` is untouched, so no `gen:api-surface` artifact is owed. Check-run `Check Changeset`: success. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

Report 6716292410: `open_questions` is empty — nothing to answer. Flags and deviations, each answered:

- **NOT MEASURED `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`** — covered by the head's `Build Core` job (`ci.yml`, step "Every published require entry point actually loads", blocking). At render time that job was still `in_progress`; its conclusion is the gate verdict and the seat reads it before landing.
- **NOT MEASURED `check:i18n`** — covered by the head's `Type Check · consumer gates` job (`lint.yml`, step "Check generated translation bundles are in sync with the schema"). The job concluded `success` and the step itself concluded `success` (read off the job's steps, since the step is `continue-on-error: true` and the job's conclusion alone would not carry it). The diff adds no translation key and no bundle entry point.
- **Deviation: eslint over changed files, not `pnpm lint` per package** — the head's `Lint · ESLint` and the scoped lint jobs are the verdict; the ones concluded are green.
- **Deviation: fix commit made with `--no-verify`** — the pre-push hooks ran on push (report), and every hook-mirrored gate also runs in CI on the head; nothing in the diff is a hook-only check.
- **Out of scope (dev): the UI consumer card was not searched for** — escalated to the seat: triage 6715940083 keeps `pm:blocking` because #31216 waits on this card, which is the consumer the card body names ("filed alongside"); the seat confirms that is the widget card.
- **PR state** — the report says `pr_create` opened #31336 as a draft; the seat marks it ready before the queue.
- **Check-runs on `94ee3ead`** (62 at last read): 27 `success`, 8 `skipped` (opt-in and path-filtered jobs), 0 `failure`/`cancelled`/`timed_out`; 27 still `in_progress` at render (`Test Core` 1–8, `Type Check · workspace`, `Build Core`, `Type Check UI`, `Test UI` 1–16). Green so far include `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Check PR Size`, `Spec property liveness`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`.
